Incorporating the July 2021 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, the policy statement’s cautiously positive tone is reinforced by strengthening credit dynamics. Domestic banks reported stronger demand for C&I loans across large, middle-market, and small firms, higher borrower inquiries, and easing terms for C&I credit, while banks also eased standards for consumer loans (credit card, auto, and other categories). U.S. branches and agencies of foreign banks similarly reported stronger C&I loan demand, citing needs tied to inventories, accounts receivable, plant and equipment, and M&A, with terms generally unchanged abroad. These SLOOS signals point to more accommodative bank credit supply and firmer loan demand than the policy statement alone implies, validating the Fed’s assessment of strengthening activity and supporting the “taper soon” guidance. Balancing this against the still-elevated vulnerabilities highlighted by the financial stability lens (stretched asset valuations, elevated business debt and CRE stress, and nonbank funding risks), the overall tone shifts from cautiously positive to moderately positive.
